label: Show invalid savegames
summary: Runs the action of the load screen's button for showing savegames that are marked invalid.
details: The game's GUI calls it from a click handler in the frontend load screen. Going by its name, it switches the list of invalid savegames on or off; the game documents nothing more.

label: After continue fade
summary: Runs a follow-up step when an animation in the main menu finishes.
details: Vanilla calls it in the on_finish of an animation in the main menu GUI. Going by its name, it comes after a fade that belongs to the Continue sequence; what exactly it does is not documented.

label: Before continue save check
summary: Runs a step when an animation in the main menu starts.
details: Vanilla calls it in the on_start of an animation in the main menu GUI. Going by its name, it checks the save before Continue goes on; the game documents nothing more.

label: The load view itself
summary: The load screen object itself, going by its name.
details: Going by its name and by how Self is used on other types, it gives back the object it is called on. No game line uses it on this type.

label: Showing invalid savegames
summary: Whether the load screen is set to show invalid savegames.
details: Vanilla uses it as the checked state of an element in the load screen, so it tells whether that option is currently on. The same file has a click action named OnShowInvalidSavegames, which presumably switches it.

label: Challenge achievements
summary: A list of achievements for the main menu's challenge section.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source (datamodel) of a list in the main menu GUI. Going by its name, the items are achievements tied to the challenge; the return type is not documented.

label: Load view
summary: Gives the load screen object that belongs to the main menu.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the main menu, so the elements inside can call the load screen's functions. It returns a FrontEndLoadView.

label: The main menu itself
summary: The main menu view itself, going by its name.
details: Going by its name and the way AccessSelf is used on widgets (to pass the widget on), it gives back the object it is called on. No game line uses it on this type.

label: Menu background
summary: The picture used as the main menu's background.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of an element in the main menu GUI.

label: Challenge character
summary: The character currently offered by the main menu's challenge section.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a block in the main menu, so the block can show that character. The return type is not documented.

label: Challenge character portrait
summary: A rendered portrait picture of the challenge character for the main menu.
details: Vanilla calls it with an environment name ('environment_bookmarks_map'), a camera name ('camera_shoulders') and the size of the widget, and uses the result as a portrait texture. The meaning of the three values is read from that one use.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The environment (scene setup) the portrait is rendered in; vanilla passes a name.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The camera that frames the portrait.

fields.name: Arg2
fields.text: The size of the widget the portrait is drawn into.

label: DLC collection
summary: The collection of the game's DLCs, as the main menu knows it.
details: Vanilla chains it with GetDlcs to get the list of DLCs and uses that as the data of a list in the main menu. It returns a DlcCollection.

label: Heir age
summary: The age of the heir character shown in the main menu, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla compares it with 1 to decide which picture to show: one version when the age is above 1 and another when it is 1 or less. Going by that use, a value of 1 or less stands for a child.

label: Heir portrait
summary: A rendered portrait picture of the heir character for the main menu.
details: Vanilla calls it with a camera name, the widget's size and a yes flag, and uses the result as a portrait texture; a separate camera is used for a child (the 'sitting_child' one). The meaning of the flag is not documented.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The camera that frames the portrait.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The size of the widget the portrait is drawn into.

fields.name: Arg2
fields.text: A yes/no flag; the game does not say what it does.

label: Main character age
summary: The age of the main character shown in the main menu, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla compares it with 1 to choose between two pictures: one when the age is above 1, another when it is 1 or less. Going by that use, a value of 1 or less stands for a child.

label: Main character portrait
summary: A rendered portrait picture of the main character for the main menu.
details: Vanilla calls it with a camera name, the widget's size and a yes flag, and uses the result as a portrait texture; a separate camera is used for a child. The meaning of the flag is not documented.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The camera that frames the portrait.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The size of the widget the portrait is drawn into.

fields.name: Arg2
fields.text: A yes/no flag; the game does not say what it does.

label: Secondary character age
summary: The age of the secondary character shown in the main menu, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla compares it with 1 to choose between two pictures: one when the age is above 1, another when it is 1 or less. Going by that use, a value of 1 or less stands for a child.

label: Secondary character portrait
summary: A rendered portrait picture of the secondary character for the main menu.
details: Vanilla calls it with a camera name, the widget's size and a yes flag, and uses the result as a portrait texture; a separate camera is used for a child. The meaning of the flag is not documented.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The camera that frames the portrait.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The size of the widget the portrait is drawn into.

fields.name: Arg2
fields.text: A yes/no flag; the game does not say what it does.

label: Subscription status text
summary: The text that tells the player the state of their subscription.
details: Vanilla uses it as the text of a label in the main menu. What a subscription state can be is not shown in the input.

label: Next challenge character
summary: Moves the main menu's challenge section on to the next challenge character.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click. Going by its name, it pairs with the 'previous' action.

label: Previous challenge character
summary: Moves the main menu's challenge section back to the previous challenge character.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click. Going by its name, it pairs with the 'next' action.

label: Steam is available
summary: Whether Steam is available to the game.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility of an element in the main menu.

label: Content
summary: A main menu action named for the game's content; no game file uses it.
details: Going by its name it is the action of a content button, but the game documents nothing more and no vanilla line calls it.

label: Continue
summary: A main menu action named for the Continue button; no game line calls it on this type.
details: The only related line in vanilla calls FrontEndLoadView.OnContinue for the Continue button, so the real button may use that one instead. The game documents nothing more.

label: Show credits
summary: Runs the main menu's Credits button.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click. Going by its name, it opens the game's credits.

label: Host a game
summary: Runs the main menu's Host button.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click. Going by its name, it starts hosting a multiplayer game; the game documents nothing more.

label: Load game
summary: Runs the main menu's Load button.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click. Going by its name, it opens the load screen.

label: Log in
summary: Runs the main menu's Login button.
details: Vanilla calls it from three button clicks in the main menu. Going by its name, it starts the login to the player's online account; the game documents nothing more.

label: Multiplayer
summary: Runs the main menu's Multiplayer button.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click. Going by its name, it opens the multiplayer menu.

label: New game
summary: Runs the main menu's New Game button.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click. Going by its name, it starts the setup of a new game.

label: Nudge
summary: A main menu action named 'nudge'; no game file uses it.
details: The game documents nothing more and no vanilla line calls it, so what it does is unknown.

label: Open Discord link
summary: Opens the game's Discord link from the main menu.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click. Going by its name, it opens the Discord address in the player's browser.

label: Open YouTube link
summary: Opens the game's YouTube link from the main menu.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click. Going by its name, it opens the YouTube address in the player's browser.

label: Quit
summary: Runs the main menu's Quit button.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click. Going by its name, it closes the game.

label: Settings
summary: Runs the main menu's Settings button.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click. Going by its name, it opens the settings.

label: Subscription
summary: Runs the main menu's subscription button.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click. Going by its name, it handles the player's subscription; the game documents nothing more.

label: The main menu itself
summary: The main menu view itself, going by its name.
details: Going by its name and by how Self is used on other types, it gives back the object it is called on. No game line uses it on this type.

label: Holding for characters
summary: Whether the main menu is holding for its characters; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla uses it to fade an element (alpha 0 when true, 1 when false) and to hide elements while it is true. Going by its name, it stays true until the character pictures are ready.

label: Showing challenge character
summary: Whether the main menu shows the challenge character.
details: Vanilla uses it to move an element between two positions (-250,0 when true, 0,0 when false) and, together with not holding for characters, to make the challenge section visible.

label: Showing heir
summary: Whether the main menu shows the heir character.
details: Vanilla combines it with the heir's age: one element is shown when the age is above 1, another when it is 1 or less.

label: Showing secondary character
summary: Whether the main menu shows the secondary character.
details: Vanilla combines it with that character's age: one element is shown when the age is above 1, another when it is 1 or less.

label: Start with challenge character
summary: Starts a game as the challenge character shown in the main menu.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click in the main menu's challenge section. The game documents nothing more than the name.

label: The multiplayer menu itself
summary: The multiplayer menu view itself, going by its name.
details: Going by its name and the way AccessSelf is used on widgets, it gives back the object it is called on. No game line uses it on this type.

label: Back
summary: Runs the Back button of the multiplayer menu.
details: Vanilla calls it from button clicks in two multiplayer GUI files. Going by its name, it leaves the multiplayer menu.

label: Host a game
summary: Runs the Host button of the multiplayer menu.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click. Going by its name, it starts hosting a multiplayer game; the game documents nothing more.

label: Load game
summary: Runs the Load button of the multiplayer menu.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click. Going by its name, it loads a saved game for multiplayer.

label: New game
summary: A multiplayer menu action named for a new game; no game line calls it on this type.
details: The only similar line in vanilla calls FrontEndMainView.OnNewGame in the main menu. Going by its name it starts a new game, but the game documents nothing more.

label: The multiplayer menu itself
summary: The multiplayer menu view itself, going by its name.
details: Going by its name and by how Self is used on other types, it gives back the object it is called on. No game line uses it on this type.

label: The front end itself
summary: The front end view (the menus before a game starts) itself, going by its name.
details: Going by its name and the way AccessSelf is used on widgets, it gives back the object it is called on. No game line uses it on this type.

label: The front end itself
summary: The front end view (the menus before a game starts) itself, going by its name.
details: Going by its name and by how Self is used on other types, it gives back the object it is called on. No game line uses it on this type.

label: The phase itself
summary: The possible future phase of a situation, itself, going by its name.
details: Going by its name and the way AccessSelf is used on widgets, it gives back the object it is called on. No game line uses it on this type.

label: Phase progress
summary: How far a possible future phase of a situation has progressed towards its takeover, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it as 'progress / takeover points' and as 'progress / takeover days', so the unit follows the kind of takeover.

label: Relative phase progress
summary: The progress of a possible future phase as a share of what it needs.
details: Vanilla uses it as the value of an element in the dynastic cycle window (likely a bar). It is a fixed-point number; the sibling that gives a percentage is GetRelativeProgressPercent.

label: Phase progress percent
summary: The progress of a possible future phase as a whole-number percentage.
details: Vanilla shows it with the percent format in the silk road texts ('Progress towards ...') and as the value of an element in the Christian church window.

label: Takeover duration in days
summary: The number of days a possible future phase needs for a takeover that is based on duration.
details: Vanilla shows it as 'progress / days' for phases with that kind of takeover.

label: Takeover points
summary: The number of points a possible future phase needs for a takeover that is based on points.
details: Vanilla shows it as 'progress / points' in the situation window.

label: Phase type
summary: The type of a possible future phase of a situation.
details: Vanilla chains it with GetName to print the phase's name, for example in 'Progress towards ...' and 'Potential Era'. The return type is not documented.

label: Takeover by duration
summary: Whether the phase takes over after a number of days.
details: Vanilla uses it to decide whether the duration display is visible, in the situation window and its debug version.

label: Takeover by points
summary: Whether the phase takes over once it has collected enough points.
details: Vanilla uses it to decide whether the points display is visible, in the situation window and its debug version.

label: The phase itself
summary: The possible future phase itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it as an argument, for example to a function that lists the catalysts for the selected phase and to one that gives the latest catalyst history of a phase.

label: Locked achievement picture
summary: A picture tied to the locked state of an achievement, going by its name; the game documents nothing more.
details: No game line uses it, so the details are unknown.

label: The achievement itself
summary: The achievement item itself, going by its name.
details: Going by its name and the way AccessSelf is used on widgets, it gives back the object it is called on. No game line uses it on this type.

label: Achievement picture
summary: The picture (icon) of the achievement.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of elements in the main menu and in the achievements GUI file.

label: Achievement
summary: The achievement behind this item.
details: Vanilla chains it with IsUnlocked, to show an achievement only when it is unlocked, to dim it (alpha 1.0 or 0.5) and to choose the 'unlocked' or 'locked' tooltip text. The return type is not documented.

label: Achievement description
summary: The description text of the achievement.
details: Vanilla uses it as the text of a label and inside the challenge achievement tooltip.

label: Achievement unlock text
summary: The text that tells what happened when the achievement was earned.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the achievements GUI file. Going by its name, the text describes the event that earned it; the game documents nothing more.

label: Achievement name
summary: The name of the achievement.
details: Vanilla uses it as the text of labels in the achievements GUI file and the achievement popup, and in the challenge tooltip.

label: Is possible
summary: Whether the achievement can currently be earned.
details: Vanilla shows an element when this is false (Not), so something marks achievements that are not possible. The exact conditions are not documented.

label: Click achievement
summary: Runs the action for clicking an achievement popup.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click handler in the achievement popup. What it does is not documented.

label: Remove achievement popup
summary: Removes the achievement item.
details: Vanilla calls it in the on_finish of an animation of the achievement popup. Going by its name, the popup goes away after it has been shown.

label: The achievement itself
summary: The achievement item itself, going by its name.
details: Going by its name and by how Self is used on other types, it gives back the object it is called on. No game line uses it on this type.

label: The alert itself
summary: The alert item (a HUD notification) itself, going by its name.
details: Going by its name and the way AccessSelf is used on widgets, it gives back the object it is called on. No game line uses it on this type.

label: Alert added
summary: Reports that the alert's adding step has finished.
details: Vanilla calls it in the on_finish of animations in the notification templates. Going by its name, it marks the end of the appearing animation; the game documents nothing more.

label: End alert animation
summary: Ends the alert's animation.
details: Vanilla calls it in the on_finish of the notification templates' animations. Going by its name, it closes the animation step; the game documents nothing more.

label: Important action
summary: The important action the alert stands for.
details: No game line uses it on this type; a similar line on another type uses it as a data context. The return type is not documented.

label: Important action type
summary: The type of the important action the alert stands for.
details: Vanilla chains it with GetIcon to get the alert's icon texture.

label: Alert tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the alert.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of the alert in the notification templates.

label: Alert is added
summary: Whether the alert has been added to the HUD.
details: Vanilla uses it as the trigger_when of an animation, so the animation starts when it turns true.

label: Alert is appearing
summary: Whether the alert is currently being added.
details: Vanilla uses it as the trigger_when of an animation, so the animation starts while the alert appears.

label: Alert is disappearing
summary: Whether the alert is currently being removed.
details: Vanilla uses it as the trigger_when of an animation, so the animation starts while the alert goes away.

label: Click alert
summary: Runs the action for clicking the alert.
details: Vanilla calls it from the onclick of the notification templates. What it does is not documented.

label: Right-click alert
summary: Runs the action for right-clicking the alert.
details: Vanilla calls it from the onrightclick of the notification templates. What it does is not documented.

label: Play alert sound
summary: Plays a sound for the alert.
details: Vanilla calls it when an animation starts, passing the widget itself (PdxGuiWidget.Self). Going by its name, it is the sound for showing the alert.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The widget the sound belongs to.

label: Alert removed
summary: Reports that the alert's removing step has finished.
details: Vanilla calls it in the on_finish of an animation in the notification templates. Going by its name, it marks the end of the disappearing animation; the game documents nothing more.

label: The alert itself
summary: The alert item itself, going by its name.
details: Going by its name and by how Self is used on other types, it gives back the object it is called on. No game line uses it on this type.

label: Start alert animation
summary: Starts the alert's animation.
details: Vanilla calls it in the on_start of animations in the notification templates. Going by its name, it starts the alert's animation; the game documents nothing more.

label: The building item itself
summary: The building slot item itself, going by its name.
details: Going by its name and the way AccessSelf is used on widgets, it gives back the object it is called on. No game line uses it on this type.

label: Can construct building
summary: Whether a building can be constructed in this slot.
details: No game line uses it on this type; vanilla uses the same name on a holding type item as the enabled and visible state of elements in the county view. The explanation rests on the name.

label: Can upgrade
summary: Whether the building in this slot can be upgraded.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility of an element, and its opposite, together with 'not ruined', as the visibility of another element in the county view and the ledger.

label: Can upgrade primary building
summary: Whether the primary building can be upgraded.
details: No game line uses it, so the details are unknown; the explanation rests on the name.

label: Cancel construction
summary: Cancels the construction in this slot.
details: No game line uses it on this type; vanilla uses a command of the same name on a domicile (CreateCommandPopup( Domicile.CancelConstruction )). The explanation rests on the name.

label: Disabled building text
summary: The text that says why the building is disabled.
details: No game line uses it, so the details are unknown; the explanation rests on the name.

label: Ruined building text
summary: The text that describes the building's ruin.
details: No game line uses it, so the details are unknown; the explanation rests on the name.

label: Construction progress
summary: How far the construction in this slot has come.
details: Vanilla uses it as the value of elements in the county view (likely progress bars). It is a fixed-point number.

label: Current or constructing building
summary: The building in this slot, or the one being built there.
details: Vanilla chains it with the building's icon, level and so on. The game's own name misspells 'Constructing'; write it as given. It returns a Building.

label: Level frame
summary: The number of the picture frame for the building's level.
details: No game line uses it. Going by its name and its whole-number type, it picks a frame of a level icon.

label: Level picture
summary: The picture used for the building's level.
details: No game line uses it. The explanation rests on the name.

label: Building tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the building slot.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of building elements in the county view.

label: Tooltip parent anchor
summary: A whole number for where the tooltip attaches to its parent element.
details: No game line uses it. Going by its name, it is the anchor setting of the tooltip.

label: Tooltip widget anchor
summary: A whole number for which point of the tooltip is attached.
details: No game line uses it. Going by its name, it is the anchor setting of the tooltip itself.

label: Controls building
summary: Whether the viewer has control of the building.
details: No game line uses it. The explanation rests on the name; who the viewer is is not documented.

label: Has level
summary: Whether the building slot has a building with a level.
details: Vanilla uses it to show level elements, and its opposite for the 'build new' icon of an empty slot.

label: Has potential building
summary: Whether a building could potentially be built in the slot.
details: Vanilla uses it to decide visibility in the ledger window.

label: Build-new icon shown
summary: Whether the icon for building something new is shown.
details: Vanilla combines it with the building button being enabled and the slot having no level, to show the build-new icon.

label: Building button enabled
summary: Whether the building button can be clicked.
details: Vanilla uses it as the enabled state of building buttons and in the build-new icon check.

label: Building button shown
summary: Whether the building button is shown.
details: No game line uses it. The explanation rests on the name.

label: Building is disabled
summary: Whether the building is disabled.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a disabled marker in the county view (there with a check that the item is the holding itself) and in the ledger.

label: Building is ruined
summary: Whether the building is in ruins.
details: Vanilla uses it to show an element in the county view; another element is shown only when the building can not be upgraded and is not ruined.

label: Building slot shown
summary: Whether the building slot is shown.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility of slots in the county view and the ledger.

label: Is under construction
summary: Whether something is being built in this slot.
details: Vanilla combines it with whether the slot has a level: shown when there is a level and construction is running, or when there is a level and none is running. Going by that, the first case is an upgrade.

label: Is highlighted
summary: Whether the building slot is highlighted.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed (down) state of an element in the county view. A ledger line with it is commented out, with the note that all of them get highlighted.

label: Click building
summary: Runs the action for clicking the building slot.
details: Vanilla calls it from the onclick of building elements in the county view and the ledger. What it does is not documented.

label: The building item itself
summary: The building slot item itself, so it can be handed on or compared.
details: Vanilla compares it with the holding itself (ObjectsEqual( GUIBuildingItem.Self, Holding.Self )).

label: The county holding itself
summary: The county holding item itself, going by its name.
details: Going by its name and the way AccessSelf is used on widgets, it gives back the object it is called on. No game line uses it on this type.

label: Holding
summary: The holding behind this county view tab.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a block in the county view, and in the tab tooltip to get the holding's name and province. It returns a Holding.

label: Is selected
summary: Whether this holding is the one currently selected in the county view.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed (down) state of the tab.

label: Click holding
summary: Runs the action for clicking the holding's tab in the county view.
details: Vanilla calls it from an onclick. Going by its name and by IsSelected, it selects the holding.

label: The county holding itself
summary: The county holding item itself, going by its name.
details: Going by its name and by how Self is used on other types, it gives back the object it is called on. No game line uses it on this type.

label: The unity stage itself
summary: The house unity stage item itself, going by its name.
details: Going by its name and the way AccessSelf is used on widgets, it gives back the object it is called on. No game line uses it on this type.

label: House unity stage
summary: The house unity stage behind this item.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a block in the house window. It returns a HouseUnityStage.

label: Marker position
summary: The position of the unity marker for this stage.
details: Vanilla uses it as the position of an element in the house window, passing the widget itself. It returns a 2D position.

label: Modifier description
summary: The text describing the modifiers of this unity stage.
details: Vanilla uses it as the whole tooltip text of a house unity stage.

label: Stage value
summary: The value of the unity stage, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the house window. Going by its name, it is the stage's number or threshold.

label: Stage weight
summary: The weight of the unity stage, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla uses it as the horizontal layout stretch factor, so a stage with a larger weight gets more width in its layout.

label: Is active
summary: Whether this unity stage is the active one.
details: Vanilla uses it, with whether the stage is valid, to show one version of the stage when it is active and another when it is not.

label: The unity stage itself
summary: The house unity stage item itself, going by its name.
details: Going by its name and by how Self is used on other types, it gives back the object it is called on. No game line uses it on this type.

label: The potential building itself
summary: The potential building item itself, going by its name.
details: Going by its name and the way AccessSelf is used on widgets, it gives back the object it is called on. No game line uses it on this type.

label: Can afford cost
summary: Whether the given character can pay the building's cost.
details: Vanilla passes the player (GetPlayer.Self) and shows an element when the answer is no.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character whose purse is checked.

label: Can construct
summary: Whether this building can be constructed.
details: Vanilla uses it as the enabled state of the build button in the county view.

label: Construct
summary: Starts the construction of this building.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click on the build button in the county view. Going by its name, that is the point where the building is ordered.

label: Building
summary: The building this item stands for.
details: Vanilla chains it with the building's icon, name and description in the county view. It returns a Building.

label: Construction time
summary: How long the construction takes.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a block in the county view. The return type is not documented.

label: Construction cost
summary: What the building costs to construct.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a block in the county view. The return type is not documented.

label: Level icon
summary: The icon for the building's level.
details: No game line uses it. The explanation rests on the name.

label: Level icon frame
summary: The number of the picture frame of the level icon.
details: No game line uses it. Going by its name and its whole-number type, it picks a frame of the icon.

label: Piety cost
summary: The piety cost of constructing the building.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a block in the county view. Going by its name, it is the piety cost; the return type is not documented.

label: Prestige cost
summary: The prestige cost of constructing the building.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a block in the county view. Going by its name, it is the prestige cost; the return type is not documented.

label: Potential building tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the potential building.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of the building element in the county view.

label: Has cost
summary: Whether the building has a cost.
details: Vanilla uses it to decide whether the cost display is visible.

label: Has piety cost
summary: Whether the building costs piety.
details: Vanilla uses it to decide whether the piety cost display is visible.

label: Has prestige cost
summary: Whether the building costs prestige.
details: Vanilla uses it to decide whether the prestige cost display is visible.

label: The potential building itself
summary: The potential building item itself, going by its name.
details: Going by its name and by how Self is used on other types, it gives back the object it is called on. No game line uses it on this type.

label: Show details
summary: Shows the details of the building.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click in the county view. Going by its name, it opens a detail view; the game documents nothing more.

label: The track item itself
summary: The track item itself, going by its name.
details: Going by its name and the way AccessSelf is used on widgets, it gives back the object it is called on. No game line uses it on this type.

label: Can afford next cost
summary: Whether the given character can pay the cost of the next step.
details: Vanilla passes the player (GetPlayer.Self) and shows an element when the answer is no.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character whose purse is checked.

label: Can afford selected cost
summary: Whether the given character can pay the cost of the selected building.
details: Vanilla passes the player (GetPlayer.Self) and shows an element when the answer is no.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character whose purse is checked.

label: Can cancel
summary: Whether the current construction can be cancelled.
details: Vanilla uses it as the enabled state of a button, and together with CanReplace to decide whether the cancel or replace button is shown for the selected building that is not being constructed.

label: Can construct next building
summary: Whether the next building in the track can be constructed.
details: Vanilla uses it as the enabled state of a button in the county view.

label: Can construct selected building
summary: Whether the selected building can be constructed.
details: Vanilla shows an element when the answer is no.

label: Can replace
summary: Whether the current building can be replaced.
details: Vanilla uses it, together with whether the current building is selected, to show a replace button; it is also combined with CanCancel there.
